name: Illinois

laws.cite: Illinois Information Technology Accessibility Act, 30 ILCS 587 (P.A. 95-307; amended by P.A. 103-729)
laws.summary: IT that the State develops, buys or provides must be accessible and meet published state standards.

laws.cite: 28 C.F.R. Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web and mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by DOJ interim final rule 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: State and local governments must make web content and mobile apps conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.

applies_to: All State entities: executive, legislative and judicial branches, constitutional offices, public bodies and public universities. Not local governments, school districts or community colleges.

deadlines.what: IITAA 2.1 (WCAG 2.1 AA) applies to IT developed, procured or substantially modified after this date
DoIT must review and amend the standards in calendar year 2026, then at least every 3 years
Federal ADA Title II floor: public entities with population 50,000+ must meet WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24)
Federal ADA Title II floor: entities under 50,000 and special districts (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: Conform to IITAA 2.1 (WCAG 2.1 A/AA, Section 508 functional and hardware criteria)
State entities must add amended standards to procurement policies within 6 months
IT from before 2024-06-24 stays under IITAA 2.0 (WCAG 2.0 AA)
mobile: implied — software and applications are covered through Section 508-based chapters; mobile apps are not named.
procurement: Recommended contract clause requires IITAA compliance; vendors provide a VPAT/ACR (508, WCAG or INT editions); a demo of accessibility features may be required.
enforcement: No private right of action in the statute sections read (5–25); questions and complaints go to DoIT.Accessibility@illinois.gov.
notes: The statutory 2026 review may produce updated standards (for example WCAG 2.2) that were not visible as of the as_of date. Section 30 and later sections of 30 ILCS 587 were not read. Federal floor: ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA, web + mobile apps) applies to all state and local government regardless of state law; DOJ's 2026-04-20 interim final rule moved compliance dates to 2027-04-26 / 2028-04-26.
